correctness.rationale: Removing any single vertex leaves the book connected, and the sole blue vertex has at least two neighbors in that component; no first PSD force is possible. From both spine vertices blue, each white page is a separate edge and can be forced from an endpoint. From a same-page pair, the two blue page vertices can force the spine. From {a,x_i} use x_i→y_i→b, and from {a,y_i} first force the isolated white x_i from a, then force b from y_i. Exchanging sides covers the other spine–page pairs. From two different pages, the white spine edge remains and every residual white page fragment attaches to it; each blue page vertex has both neighbors in that one white component. Thus neither can start a force. The categories are exhaustive and disjoint, giving 1+n+4n minima after excluding both the empty set and singletons. The argument also covers n=1: the four-cycle has all six pairs as minima, and there are no different-page pairs.
residual_risks: The accompanying checker recomputes white components after every force and compares all singletons and pairs for 1≤n≤12. It was not run; correctness here is established by the symbolic proof, not an assertion of an independent finite replay.

evidence: The partial-2-tree theorem equates Z_+, PSD maximum nullity and induced-tree cover number. The book embeds in a 2-tree by adding x_i onto edge ab and y_i onto x_i b, then deleting all added x_i b edges. Its two layers are induced stars and a page gives a cycle, so the tree-cover number is exactly two.

Propositions 3.1–3.2 compare forcing under degree-two suppression; they supply transferable forcing sets or cardinality equalities, not a parametric census of every initial pair in this graph. The 2013 author abstract asserts any vertex can be included in some minimum set, not that all pairs can be prescribed. The catalogue wheels result is for another graph family.
broader_coverage.reasoning: Prior general theorems recover the scalar and provide operations for analyzing particular starts. None of the inspected statements supplies both the positive same-page/spine cases and the obstruction for every pair on different pages.

evidence: The componentwise rule permits multiple fires from one spine vertex into distinct white pages. A different-page pair leaves one connected white component with two neighbors of each blue vertex, an obstruction not expressed by the scalar or an existence theorem for containing individual vertices.

The degree-two reduction treats membership and shifts a selected degree-two vertex when necessary to establish a minimum size; it does not identify which of the original pairs result in success. Reversing its comparisons would still require analyzing the candidate configurations.
claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: The new part is exhaustiveness with respect to fixed locations of both initial vertices. Deriving that from the general framework requires a book-specific analysis, not substituting a graph size into a prior coverage theorem.

evidence: The quadrilateral book is the same graph: a spine edge in parallel with n internally disjoint paths of length three. The skew-forcing record uses exactly this graph, but it requires meeting both bipartition classes, with (n+1)^2 minimum sets. The paired-domination record also uses this graph, but studies a different invariant.

For n≥2, the PSD minima cannot be transferred from matroid bases: replacing an element of one same-page pair by either element of another same-page pair gives an excluded cross-page pair, violating basis exchange.
equivalent_formulations.reasoning: The book aliases identify the graph but do not identify the forcing rule. In particular, PSD forcing admits even the same-bipartition spine–page pairs; its minimum family is not the pair family of the skew rule or a matroid-basis enumeration.

checked_sources: Ekstrand et al. (2012), Theorem 3.3; related skew and PSD catalogue findings
value.rationale: The classification resolves a location-sensitive question that the known minimum size cannot answer on a standard graph product: putting both vertices on different pages fails completely, whereas a spine vertex can be partnered with any other vertex. Together the cases give the leading PSD forcing-polynomial coefficient and a labeled census useful for testing structural guesses about minimum sets. This is a natural complete classification with a cone-of-pairs obstruction, not a finite recomputation of the scalar.
residual_risks: The result classifies only minimum starts; it does not determine the rest of the PSD forcing polynomial or propagation times.
